extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, patent practitioners, applicants, industry stakeholders, and Congress
extracted.subtask_description: An annual report from the Patent Public Advisory Committee (PPAC) providing recommendations, criteria, and assessments for USPTO rulemaking, fee setting, patent examination quality and pendency, PTAB matters, AI impacts, IT modernization, and outreach/education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six key PPAC focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC and the USPTO have focused our collective efforts on six (6) key areas: (1) linking patents and innovation to global competitiveness, (2) expanding outreach and education initiatives, (3) reducing unexamined patent application inventory without sacrificing quality, (4) closing the gap between PTAB and patent examiner patentability determinations, (5) maintaining agency financial stability, and (6) assessing the impact of AI as a tool and its impact on innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the high-level organizing framework for priorities across the report and drives recommendations in subsequent sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking process transparency and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process takes approximately one year, comprising two distinct phases– Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) and Final Rule (FR). About half a year is spent in NPRM (published with a full 60–90-day public comment period), and the Final Rule phase typically takes another half year (published with 30-60 days before Effective Date). The USPTO solicits stakeholder input at multiple stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit broad public comment, host engagement events, carefully review all comments before finalizing rules; track counts of notices and comments to demonstrate engagement (e.g., FY2024: 32 rule-related notices, hundreds of comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for analyzing aggregate fee increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the aggregate proposed fee increase involves considering the USPTO’s overall needs to fulfill its mission, including the need to maintain a robust operating reserve, prioritize expenditures (examination, IT), and account for statutory changes reducing fee revenue (e.g., UAIA discounts) and pay raises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether USPTO is prioritizing the right expenditures, operating efficiently, life-cycle costs of getting/maintaining a patent, incentive effects on applicants, and impact on small inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of individual fee changes: fairness & applicant behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fee increases and newly introduced fees should be judged based on fairness, their effect on applicant behavior, and whether they are likely to raise expected revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether fees place undue burdens (especially on small entities/independent inventors), whether revenues will be used predominantly for examination/related services, and whether fees alter filing/prosecution incentives in undesirable ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for targeted fee increases only when tied to examiner/examination resources
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports certain fee increases (e.g., excess claims, IDS, RCE tiering, AIA trial fees) only when there is confidence additional revenue will support examination quality or directly offset USPTO costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees increase, ensure funds are dedicated to examiners' time, tools, or processes that improve patent reliability; seek public assurance that fee increases will not be diverted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to across-the-board increases that unduly burden small inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC does not support front‑loaded across-the-board fee increases that place undue burdens on individual inventors and small businesses (the second 5% across-the-board increase was explicitly opposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mechanisms that disproportionately impact small/micro entities; consider distributional impacts when structuring revenue changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP‑a (After Final Consideration Pilot) fee design principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC views this fee as problematic as it requires paying the fee without any guarantee of an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals: (a) Don’t require a fee unless you can guarantee the applicant will get an interview, or (b) Don’t pay the fee until the applicant does get an interview. If one of these is enacted, PPAC would support the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment recordation should not be cost-prohibitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment recordation increases were proposed to reduce frivolous submissions, but the PPAC is against imposing a fee that would impede transparency of ownership because transparency is key to patent data integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fees that deter timely updating of assignment data; balance deterrence of frivolous filings with need for accurate public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing application fee timing principle
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports a fee on continuing applications with modification: drop the year-three provision and only make applicable for year 7 or after because three years may be too short (e.g., PCT route or backlog areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set timing thresholds that account for prosecution realities and avoid penalizing legitimate, early continuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent fee and pendency priority
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC does not agree with proposed design patent fee increases and believes USPTO should prioritize pendency issues before applying fees; suggests considering law change (e.g., maintenance fees) instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address pendency backlog and expedited-fee burdens before adding new design patent fees that may saddle users already paying for speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fee conditional support
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC is supportive of excess claims fee increases with the caveat that the public wants certainty that increased fee revenue will be spent on examination and/or giving examiners more time to evaluate expanded claim sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If imposing excess-claim fees, dedicate funds to provide examiners with additional time/resources to examine excess claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time (EOT) for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC is supportive of decreasing EOT fees for provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce barriers to provisional filers; fee structure should encourage timely provisional filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) fee support with examiner-time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC is supportive of IDS fee increases, but notes that if additional fees are paid, the money should go towards allowing examiners more time to consider the additional references. Also recommends legislative reform of inequitable conduct to reduce over-citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link IDS fees to examiner workload adjustments and consider broader legal changes that reduce defensive over‑disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) fee fairness principle
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC generally supports PTA fee to cover USPTO cost of a patentee requesting adjustment, with the caveat: if USPTO made the adjustment mistake, applicant shouldn’t have to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between applicant- and USPTO-caused adjustments when imposing user fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Extension (PTE) fee proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports PTE fee increases in principle but urges USPTO to consider whether a large jump in fees is optimal, particularly the initial fee given start-up companies may be resource constrained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate PTE fees to avoid disproportionate burden on resource-constrained entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) cost-recovery principle
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports raising RCE fees and splitting later RCEs into higher tiers so that costs of continued examinations are recovered directly from applicants requesting multiple RCEs, rather than subsidized by others. The proposal continues to set the first RCE below cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tiered pricing to align user payments with service costs and discourage excessive serial RCEs while preserving reasonable first-RCE access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action: tiered fee to encourage efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports tiered fees for suspension of action (higher charges for subsequent suspensions) to encourage efficient applicant behavior; fees for suspensions requested at time of filing CPA or RCE would not be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tiers so they discourage unnecessary delays but do not penalize legitimate prosecution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer fee opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC does not support a fee increase for terminal disclaimers, finding that a fee will unfairly burden filers with limited resources and may pressure them to give up patent term in exchange for lower costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fees that create inequitable outcomes between well-resourced and less-resourced filers in obtaining comparable patent protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional delay petition fee tiering
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports fee increases for unintentional delay petitions; the fee design includes a higher tier for petitions with longer delays to offset USPTO processing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align petition fees with expected processing costs while considering fairness for shorter delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA trial fees should support cost recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC supports increases in AIA (IPR) trial fees due to increasing costs (court cases, inflation) and to support aggregate cost recovery for USPTO operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set trial fees to reflect true administrative costs so other fee categories need not subsidize PTAB operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to word-count fees that favor well-resourced petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC does not support a word count fee increase as it favors well-resourced petitioners; instead the USPTO should set reasonable word limits and allow requests for additional words upon showing of cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain equitable access to filing capacity; use discretionary mechanisms rather than paywalls for necessary additional briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to Director Review fees
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC does not support charging a fee for Director review of PTAB decisions; Director review should be encouraged to ensure consistency and charging may adversely affect individual inventors and small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep certain oversight/review processes accessible and not fee-restricted to preserve consistent adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency reduction strategies: examiner staffing and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce unexamined patent application inventory the USPTO should: (1) improve routing so examiners receive applications aligned with their technical/scientific training, (2) extend working hours given high telework rates, and (3) increase pay — USPTO secured an increase in the special rate table and hired over 800 new examiners this year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine better case routing, workload management, recruitment, and compensation to reduce pendency while protecting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow and organizational improvements for pendency & quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations include overhauling approach to timing and routing of newly filed applications, improving classification processes, conducting organizational assessments, and assessing other time and details to create optimum balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform systemic reviews of workflows and classification to align workload, reduce mismatches, and improve examiner effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and governance of AI/IT tools in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure IT stability and resiliency, investigate and implement AI search tools, and implement non‑production time tools for IT outages. Explore AI as a facilitative tool for enterprise workflow and as a contributor/subject matter for invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot and evaluate AI tools carefully, ensure robust IT infrastructure and devote resources to resilience, validation, and training; monitor impacts on quality and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and awards to incentivize performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance gainsharing award pilot, optimize docket management award, and create awards based on Patents‑wide goals to recognize examiner contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted awards to align incentives with strategic objectives (reduced pendency, quality metrics) while monitoring for unintended behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing the loop between examination and PTAB (study & training)
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC recommends USPTO release its 'closing the loop' study on examiner/PTAB inconsistencies, hold practitioner information and training sessions, and consider additional studies (e.g., role of expert testimony) to help close inconsistency gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical studies to inform training and process changes; provide outreach to practitioners to reduce IPR vulnerabilities of issued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 35 U.S.C. 325(d) discretionary denials to improve quality
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC recommends considering more robust use of section 325(d), with applicable rules that would encourage patent applicants to highlight a limited number of references during examination, to improve patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt rules that incentivize focused prosecution and reduce repetitive petitions that strain resources while preserving fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO as source of empirical data for policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO should continue to generate robust, accurate, and unbiased evidence (e.g., USPTO/FDA Drug Patent & Exclusivity Study) to inform intellectual property policy discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain data transparency, rigorous methods, and independent analysis to support policy decisions and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and patent subject‑matter guidance expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends the USPTO continue to explore, utilize, and advance AI as it relates to being a facilitator of invention, the subject matter of invention, and a propelling tool for enterprise effectiveness. The PPAC congratulates the AI/ET working group for issuing guidance on 'Patent Subject Matter Eligibility, Including Artificial Intelligence' but encourages developing a broader range of examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand practical examples in guidance, continue outreach, and clarify how AI affects person‑of‑ordinary‑skill standards and inventorship issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology management: modernization, cybersecurity, and user experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue IT modernization, strengthen cybersecurity (including cloud migration strategy), and perform user experience testing while remaining diligent about cost containment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance modernization and security with cost controls; test UX to ensure systems meet user needs and resilience requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and operations of advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each PAC consists of nine members who are U.S. citizens representing a broad spectrum of USPTO users; for PPAC include minimum 25% members from small entity applicants (including one independent inventor), and three leaders from recognized labor organizations; members serve three‑year terms and may be reappointed for one additional consecutive three‑year term; PPAC meets at least twice per year (typically quarterly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure diversity of representation (entity size, backgrounds), transparent appointment processes, and routine meetings to fulfill advisory role.
